sections.h2: What is Whitfield County, Georgia, and why does it matter for a tax bill?
sections.html:
Whitfield County had a July 2025 Census estimate of 106,212 residents on 290.45 square miles of land. That works out to 354.2 people per square mile in 2020. Dalton is the county seat, and Cohutta, Tunnel Hill and Varnell are the other cities.

The county's history page says Dalton was incorporated in 1847 after the Western & Atlantic Railroad arrived, and Whitfield County was formed from part of Murray County in 1851. Two major rail lines, Norfolk Southern and CSX, still meet in Dalton, and there is no passenger service. Civil War fighting around Rocky Face Ridge in 1864 and the 1,477 foot Chetoogeta Mountain tunnel at Tunnel Hill are part of the county's heritage.

  • Housing units: 40,987, with 67.0% owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $218,000.
  • Median gross rent: $971, and 409 building permits were issued in 2025.
  • Mean commute: 21.8 minutes, and 63.0% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force.
  • Median household income: $67,070 in 2024 dollars.
  • Households: 36,834, averaging 2.78 people, with 89.7% in the same house a year earlier.

sections.h2: Who bills Whitfield County property tax?
sections.html:
The Whitfield County Tax Commissioner bills and collects, at 1013 Riverburch Parkway, Dalton, GA 30721, phone (706) 275-7510, Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 4:55 pm. Payments run through the county's online tax site. The Board of Assessors determines value and keeps its own tax help website, which the county home site links.

Real property tax is typically billed in October of each tax year, based on fair market value on January 1. The commissioner's FAQ gives December 20 as the normal real estate due date, so read the date printed on your bill. Mobile homes are billed in January and are due April 1.

The county FAQ makes one distinction that matters inside Dalton. Whitfield County assesses property at 40% of fair market value, but the City of Dalton assesses at 100%. A house inside city limits therefore carries a different assessment than one in the unincorporated county, so ask the commissioner which bills apply.

sections.h2: What are the Whitfield County penalties for late tax?
sections.html:
Interest runs monthly at the Federal Bank Prime Loan percentage as of January 1 plus 3%, divided by 12. The commissioner's page gives 2025 as the example, with a prime rate of 7.50%, which produced 0.875% per month. Use that formula with the January 1 rate for the year in question, and do not assume the 2025 rate applies. An older FAQ entry on the same site mentions 1% a month and a 10% penalty after 90 days, so confirm the schedule with the office before you rely on either version.

A penalty of 5% is added every 120 days of delinquency until it reaches a 20% cap. After 120 days the office records a lien against the property and the owner with the Clerk of Court and on the General Execution Docket, adding fees of $12 and $10. The commissioner notes that liens are public, so credit bureaus may see them.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Whitfield County assessment?
sections.html:
File a written appeal within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The appeal may rest on taxability, value, uniformity or the denial of an exemption, and the amount of tax cannot be appealed. File it with the Board of Tax Assessors and state your chosen method of appeal.

State rules give three routes: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer for non-homestead real property above $500,000, or arbitration with a certified appraisal. A Board of Equalization decision can be taken to superior court by written notice within 30 days. The Georgia Department of Revenue notes that it cannot override the local boards on individual values.

Returns are filed between January 1 and April 1, and a return not filed carries the prior year's final value. The Board of Assessors mails business and personal property return forms each January. For a mobile home, the bill itself serves as the assessment notice, so the 45 days count from the mailing date of the tax bill.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions does Whitfield County offer?
sections.html:
Whitfield County lists five codes on its commissioner's site, and the application goes to the Tax Assessor. You must own and live in the home on January 1, and an application received after April 1 starts the next year. Once granted, an exemption renews each year until you move or ask for a different one.

  • S1: regular homestead, with no additional requirements.
  • S1-V: regular homestead with an additional exemption for the City of Varnell, for age 65 and income over $40,000.
  • S3: senior homestead for age 65 with spousal income under $40,000.
  • S4-7: senior homestead for age 70.
  • S5: disabled veteran exemption, with a DD-214 and a 100% disability rating.

The county FAQ adds that a homeowner reaching age 62 may apply for an additional exemption. Special assessment programs also exist for conservation use, residential transitional property, agricultural property, rehabilitated historic property, qualified timber and the Forest Land Protection Act, and each needs an application.

sections.h2: How does Whitfield County tax work when I sell a house?
sections.html:
The tax statement goes to the owner as of January 1, and the commissioner says the office does not decide who owes what after a sale. That obligation is typically settled at closing. If the office learns of a sale within 90 days of the due date and verifies the transfer, it will bill the new owner.

Deeds are recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, and the Assessors Office then updates the owner on the record. Bills are mailed to the homeowner, never to the lender, so a seller whose lender pays from escrow should still tell the servicer about the sale. Ask the commissioner for a balance on every year before closing, and confirm whether Dalton or Varnell levies apply.

faqs.q: Where is the Whitfield County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: The office is at 1013 Riverburch Parkway in Dalton, Georgia 30721. The phone number is (706) 275-7510, and hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:55 pm.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Whitfield County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. File a written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors that names your method of appeal. The tax amount itself cannot be appealed.

faqs.q: Is the Dalton assessment different from the county's?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner's FAQ says Whitfield County assesses at 40% of fair market value, while the City of Dalton assesses at 100%. Ask which applies to your address.

faqs.q: When do Whitfield County homestead applications close?
faqs.a: An application must be received before April 1 of the tax year to count for that year. A later one takes effect the next year. The home must be owned and occupied on January 1.

faqs.q: What happens to the bill if I sell during the year?
faqs.a: The statement still goes to the January 1 owner, and the obligation is typically settled at closing. If the office hears of the sale within 90 days of the due date, it bills the new owner. Mortgage companies do not receive a copy of the bill.
